# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1046
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1046
- **Title**: gh-1044 [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1044` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +534
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T13:10:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T13:10:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1044
### Root Cause

The SM merge guard's coverage probe listed validation runs with a hard `--event workflow_dispatch` filter, so green `quality.yml` runs arriving as `pull_request` events (leg push → PR synchronize → Quality) were never considered. gh-1033: the #1020 merge's tree `89755209ac7d` WAS validated green (run 39126212895 on head `32f43df1`), yet the guard alarmed "no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree". `decide()` was already event-agnostic — the discrimination lived entirely in the fetch.

### Fix

- `scripts/sm_merge_guard.py`: dropped the `--event` filter — a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`/`pull_request`/`push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree now validates it; alarm message updated accordingly. Red/in-flight runs stay rejected via the existing `conclusion == "success"` re-check.
- `.github/workflows/sm-merge-guard.yml`: runs the fixed guard from this repo instead of the canonical reusable workflow. The canonical probe lives in `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` and the factory token has no push access there (403 verified), so the script is vendored here (same pattern as `scripts/loop_guard.py`). Re-point the stub at the reusable workflow once upstream absorbs the any-event fix.

### Test Coverage

- `scripts/tests/test_sm_merge_guard.py` — 15 tests: probe fetch (no `--event` filter, any-event green runs fetched, red/in-flight excluded), `decide()` (green pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch validate; red/in-flight/uncovered alarm), and the gh-1033 replay via `--runs-json` (green pull_request run → exit 0; red or no covering run → exit 3). RED confirmed against the unfixed probe before the fix.
- CLI replay of the exact gh-1033 inputs: `ok — tree match: run 39126212895`, exit 0.
- Python: 37/37 (`scripts/tests`). Full JS unit suite: **4127 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes

- Vendoring inverts the stub's "all logic in agentic-workflows" comment out of necessity (no write access); the vendored header documents how to re-sync with upstream.
- `__pycache__/`/`*.pyc` added to `.gitignore` and two accidentally-committed `.pyc` files removed from the index.

# gh-1044: [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)

## Description

## Live evidence (2026-10-18)

Alarm gh-1033 fired on the merge of PR #1020 (main commit `d10dbcba03a1`):

> Guard verdict: no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree

**The tree WAS validated green.** PR #1020 merged head `32f43df1` (tree `89755209ac7d` = the squashed main commit tree — main had not moved). Quality run https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39126212895 covered exactly that head — **success** — but with `event: pull_request` (branch push by the conflict-rework leg → PR synchronize → Quality), not `workflow_dispatch`.

## Root cause

The guard's tree-coverage probe (gh-1537 AC5) considers only `workflow_dispatch`-event quality.yml runs. In this repo most validations arrive as `pull_request`-event runs (legs push to the PR branch, CI fires on synchronize). The merge side correctly accepted the green pull_request run (merge-validated consumed it) — the guard disagreed, so a clean, validated merge reads as "SM merged without validation".

## Fix

The guard must count a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree — or at minimum add `pull_request`. The check is about *tree coverage by a green validation*, not about *who dispatched it*.

## Why not just silence the alarm

A too-narrow coverage check cries wolf on every conflict-rework merge (legs push → pull_request CI → merge): operators learn to ignore `[sm-guard]` alarms, and the one real unvalidated merge drowns in false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the gh-1033 inputs (merged tree `89755209ac7d`, green pull_request run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1) yields NO alarm.
- [ ] A merge whose tree has NO green run of any event still alarms (true positive preserved).
- [ ] Unit test: coverage probe accepts pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch green runs alike; rejects red/in-flight runs of any event.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""SM merge guard (gh-1537 AC5) — the cheap alarm for the serialized-
+validation invariant.
+
+Invariant under watch: the SM queue (machine-sm.yml -> factory-sm) is
+strictly serialized and validates the EXACT tree that merges — update
+branch onto main, dispatch ci.yml on the updated head, merge only when
+green. With the post-merge main CI run retired (gh-1537), nothing else
+stands between a violated invariant and a red main: this guard fires on
+every push to main and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a
+SUCCESSFUL ci.yml run (an SM pre-merge validation). The covering run may
+be of ANY event — workflow_dispatch, pull_request or push (gh-1044):
+most validations in this repo arrive as pull_request-event runs (leg
+push -> PR synchronize -> CI), and the invariant is tree coverage by a
+green validation, not who dispatched it.
+
+A push whose tree has no successful validation run of any event is the
+#687-invariant violation the owner asked to alarm on instead of relying
+on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
+issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).
+
+Canonical home: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py
+(fetched at @main by the factory reusable workflow). This in-repo copy
+exists because the canonical probe filtered `--event workflow_dispatch`
+and this repo's CI validates mostly via pull_request runs (gh-1044 false
+alarm gh-1033 on the #1020 merge); the factory token cannot push to the
+workflows repo. Once upstream accepts any-event coverage, drop this copy
+and re-point .github/workflows/sm-merge-guard.yml at the reusable
+workflow.
+
+Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
+merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
+squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
+invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
+the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
+compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
+(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).
+
+Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard —
+defense-in-depth: gh-1522 retired the bump flow so none land anymore, but
+if one ever returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the full
+quality gate that runs on the cut v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.
+
+Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
+when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.
+
+Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
+so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.

+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

+# merge), so the matching run is always among the most recent dispatches;
+# the cap bounds gh api calls per push, not correctness.
+MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS = 40
+

The SM merge guard's coverage probe listed validation runs with a hard `--event workflow_dispatch` filter, so green `quality.yml` runs arriving as `pull_request` events (leg push → PR synchronize → Quality) were never considered. gh-1033: the #1020 merge's tree `89755209ac7d` WAS validated green (run 39126212895 on head `32f43df1`), yet the guard alarmed "no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree". `decide()` was already event-agnostic — the discrimination lived entirely in the fetch.

# gh-1044: [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)

## Description

## Live evidence (2026-10-18)

Alarm gh-1033 fired on the merge of PR #1020 (main commit `d10dbcba03a1`):

> Guard verdict: no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree

**The tree WAS validated green.** PR #1020 merged head `32f43df1` (tree `89755209ac7d` = the squashed main commit tree — main had not moved). Quality run https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39126212895 covered exactly that head — **success** — but with `event: pull_request` (branch push by the conflict-rework leg → PR synchronize → Quality), not `workflow_dispatch`.

## Root cause

The guard's tree-coverage probe (gh-1537 AC5) considers only `workflow_dispatch`-event quality.yml runs. In this repo most validations arrive as `pull_request`-event runs (legs push to the PR branch, CI fires on synchronize). The merge side correctly accepted the green pull_request run (merge-validated consumed it) — the guard disagreed, so a clean, validated merge reads as "SM merged without validation".

## Fix

The guard must count a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree — or at minimum add `pull_request`. The check is about *tree coverage by a green validation*, not about *who dispatched it*.

## Why not just silence the alarm

A too-narrow coverage check cries wolf on every conflict-rework merge (legs push → pull_request CI → merge): operators learn to ignore `[sm-guard]` alarms, and the one real unvalidated merge drowns in false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the gh-1033 inputs (merged tree `89755209ac7d`, green pull_request run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1) yields NO alarm.
- [ ] A merge whose tree has NO green run of any event still alarms (true positive preserved).
- [ ] Unit test: coverage probe accepts pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch green runs alike; rejects red/in-flight runs of any event.

  "fields": {
    "summary": "[sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)",
    "description": "## Live evidence (2026-10-18)

Alarm gh-1033 fired on the merge of PR #1020 (main commit `d10dbcba03a1`):

> Guard verdict: no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree

**The tree WAS validated green.** PR #1020 merged head `32f43df1` (tree `89755209ac7d` = the squashed main commit tree — main had not moved). Quality run https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39126212895 covered exactly that head — **success** — but with `event: pull_request` (branch push by the conflict-rework leg → PR synchronize → Quality), not `workflow_dispatch`.

## Root cause

The guard's tree-coverage probe (gh-1537 AC5) considers only `workflow_dispatch`-event quality.yml runs. In this repo most validations arrive as `pull_request`-event runs (legs push to the PR branch, CI fires on synchronize). The merge side correctly accepted the green pull_request run (merge-validated consumed it) — the guard disagreed, so a clean, validated merge reads as "SM merged without validation".

## Fix

The guard must count a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree — or at minimum add `pull_request`. The check is about *tree coverage by a green validation*, not about *who dispatched it*.

## Why not just silence the alarm

A too-narrow coverage check cries wolf on every conflict-rework merge (legs push → pull_request CI → merge): operators learn to ignore `[sm-guard]` alarms, and the one real unvalidated merge drowns in false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the gh-1033 inputs (merged tree `89755209ac7d`, green pull_request run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1) yields NO alarm.
- [ ] A merge whose tree has NO green run of any event still alarms (true positive preserved).
- [ ] Unit test: coverage probe accepts pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch green runs alike; rejects red/in-flight runs of any event.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39129445273) · started 12:57 · done 13:11 ✅"
  }

+exists because the canonical probe filtered `--event workflow_dispatch`
+and this repo's CI validates mostly via pull_request runs (gh-1044 false
+alarm gh-1033 on the #1020 merge); the factory token cannot push to the
+workflows repo. Once upstream accepts any-event coverage, drop this copy
+and re-point .github/workflows/sm-merge-guard.yml at the reusable
+workflow.

+the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
+compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
+(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

+defense-in-depth: gh-1522 retired the bump flow so none land anymore, but
+if one ever returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the full

+

+when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.
+

+so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
+"""

+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
+

+# Cap the per-run tree lookups: validations are fresh (minutes before the
+# merge), so the matching run is always among the most recent dispatches;
+# the cap bounds gh api calls per push, not correctness.
+MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS = 40
+
+
+def gh(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
+    proc = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
+    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
+    return proc.stdout
+
+
+def fetch_validated_runs(repo: str, workflow: str,
+                         window_hours: int) -> list:
+    """Recent SUCCESSFUL <workflow> runs of ANY event (workflow_dispatch,
+    pull_request, push), each with the tree sha of its head commit
+    resolved via the commits API.
+
+    No --event filter: the invariant is tree coverage by a green
+    validation, not who dispatched it (gh-1044 — the guard false-alarmed
+    on the #1020 merge because the green Quality run that covered the
+    tree was a pull_request-event run, dropped by the old
+    `--event workflow_dispatch` filter; most validations in this repo
+    arrive as pull_request runs: leg push -> PR synchronize -> Quality)."""
+    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=window_hours)
+    out = gh("run", "list", "--repo", repo, "--workflow", workflow,
+             "--json", "databaseId,headSha,conclusion,createdAt",
+             "--limit", "100")
+    runs = []
+    for r in json.loads(out):
+        if r.get("conclusion") != "success":
+            continue
+        created = datetime.fromisoformat(
+            r["createdAt"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
+        if created < since:
+            continue

+            "head_sha": r["headSha"],

+            # field every fetched run read as None != "success" and was
+            # skipped — the guard alarmed on every push (gh-1568).
+            "conclusion": r.get("conclusion"),
+            "tree_sha": None,  # resolved below

+            # resolves to null/empty (gh-1568: every tree match silently
+            # failed and every merge-commit landing false-alarmed).
+            tree = gh("api", f"repos/{repo}/commits/{run['head_sha']}",
+                      "--jq", ".commit.tree.sha").strip()

+            print(f"::warning::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
+    return runs

+           runs: list, workflow: str = "ci.yml") -> dict:

+    successful dispatched validations. Returns a verdict dict."""
+    if subject.startswith("chore(release):"):
+        return {"verdict": "skipped",
+                "reason": "release-bot bump push — the v* tag run gates it"}
+    for run in runs:
+        # Only successes validate — a run with NO conclusion was never
+        # confirmed green, so it can never certify a push
+        # (fetch_validated_runs pre-filters, but the test seam and any
+        # future caller may pass mixed or incomplete run dicts — the
+        # invariant holds by construction).
+        if run.get("conclusion") != "success":
+            continue
+        if run.get("head_sha") == pushed_sha:
+            return {"verdict": "ok",
+                    "reason": f"exact head-SHA match: run "
+                              f"{run.get('database_id')} validated the "
+                              f"merged commit itself (fast-forward)"}
+        if run.get("tree_sha") and run["tree_sha"] == pushed_tree:
+            return {"verdict": "ok",
+                    "reason": f"tree match: run {run.get('database_id')} "
+                              f"validated this exact tree (squash/merge "
+                              f"commit re-landed it)"}

+            "reason": f"no successful {workflow} run of any event "
+                      f"(workflow_dispatch, pull_request, push) covers "
+                      f"this tree — the SM merged without (or before) a "
+                      f"green validation of the exact tree"}
+
+
+def alarm_issue(repo: str, pushed_sha: str, subject: str, reason: str,
+                runs: list) -> None:
+    """File or update the deduplicated sm-guard issue (ci-red-report
+    convention: one open issue per guard, comments for repeats)."""
+    links = "\n".join(
+        f"- https://github.com/{repo}/actions/runs/{r.get('database_id')}"
+        f" (head `{r.get('head_sha')}`"
+        + (f", tree `{r['tree_sha']}`" if r.get("tree_sha") else "")
+        + ")"
+        for r in runs[:10])
+    # An empty commit message (git commit --allow-empty-message / the Git
+    # API) would crash the alarm itself on splitlines()[0] — the one path
+    # where the sm-guard issue would be lost for exactly the push that
+    # tripped it. Degrade to a placeholder instead.
+    subject_line = (subject.splitlines()[0]
+                    if subject.splitlines() else "(empty commit message)")
+    body = (
+        f"**Pushed SHA**: `{pushed_sha}`\n"
+        f"**Subject**: {subject_line}\n\n"
+        f"**Why this is an alarm** (gh-1537 AC5): the SM queue must be "
+        f"strictly serialized and validate the exact tree that merges. "
+        f"This push to main has no successful ci.yml validation dispatch "
+        f"covering its tree.\n\n"
+        f"**Guard verdict**: {reason}\n\n"
+        f"Recent dispatched validation runs considered:\n"
+        f"{links or '(none in the window)'}\n")
+    existing = gh("issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--state", "open",
+                  "--label", ALARM_LABEL,
+                  "--json", "number", "--jq", ".[0].number // empty")
+    if existing.strip():
+        gh("issue", "comment", existing.strip(), "--repo", repo,
+           "--body", body)
+        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: commented on #{existing.strip()}")
+    else:
+        out = gh("issue", "create", "--repo", repo,
+                 "--title", f"[sm-guard] main push without validated tree: "
+                            f"{pushed_sha[:12]}",
+                 "--body", body, "--label", "bug", "--label", ALARM_LABEL)
+        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: filed {out.strip().splitlines()[-1]}")
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    ap.add_argument("--repo", default=os.environ.get("GITHUB_REPOSITORY"))
+    ap.add_argument("--sha", required=True, help="pushed head commit sha")
+    ap.add_argument("--subject", default="",
+                    help="pushed head commit subject (first line enough)")
+    ap.add_argument("--tree", required=True,
+                    help="tree sha of the pushed head (`git rev-parse "
+                         "HEAD^{tree}`)")
+    ap.add_argument("--runs-json",
+                    help="test seam: pre-fetched validation runs "
+                         "(skip the gh run list/tree lookups)")
+    ap.add_argument("--workflow", default="ci.yml",
+                    help="validation workflow FILE name the SM dispatches "
+                         "(ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)")
+    ap.add_argument("--window-hours", type=int, default=24)
+    ap.add_argument("--alarm-issue", action="store_true",
+                    help="file/update the sm-guard issue on violation "
+                         "(needs --repo + GH_TOKEN)")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+
+    if args.runs_json:
+        with open(args.runs_json, encoding="utf-8") as f:
+            runs = json.load(f)
+    else:
+        if not args.repo:
+            print("ERROR: --repo or GITHUB_REPOSITORY required",
+                  file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+        try:
+            runs = fetch_validated_runs(args.repo, args.workflow,
+                                        args.window_hours)
+        except RuntimeError as e:
+            print(f"ERROR: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 1
+
+    verdict = decide(args.subject, args.sha, args.tree, runs,
+                     args.workflow)
+    print(f"sm-merge-guard: {verdict['verdict']} — {verdict['reason']}")
+    if verdict["verdict"] != "alarm":
+        return 0
+
+    if args.alarm_issue:
+        if not args.repo:
+            print("ERROR: --alarm-issue needs --repo", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+        try:
+            alarm_issue(args.repo, args.sha, args.subject,
+                        verdict["reason"], runs)
+        except RuntimeError as e:
+            print(f"ERROR: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 1
+    else:
+        print("::warning::alarm (issue filing disabled — pass "
+              "--alarm-issue in the workflow)")
+    return 3
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Unit tests for scripts/sm_merge_guard.py — the tree-coverage probe.
+
+Reproduces gh-1044: the guard alarmed "no successful quality.yml
+workflow_dispatch run covers this tree" on the merge of PR #1020

+tree (head 32f43df1, tree 89755209ac7d) with conclusion=success — as a

+`--event workflow_dispatch` filter.

+Coverage asserted here (ticket AC3):
+  * a green run of ANY event (workflow_dispatch / pull_request / push)
+    whose head/tree covers the merged tree VALIDATES it;
+  * red or in-flight runs of any event NEVER validate;
+  * a tree with no green run of any event still ALARMS (true positive).
+
+The gh-1033 replay values below are the real ones from the alarm issue
+and the gh-1044 ticket; all other fixtures are synthetic hex. No network,
+no gh — the probe's `gh` seam and the `--runs-json` CLI seam are used.
+
+Same public-content discipline as test_loop_guard.py: stdlib unittest
+only, runnable standalone (`python3 scripts/tests/test_sm_merge_guard.py`
+or `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`).
+"""
+import io
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from contextlib import redirect_stdout
+
+TESTS_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+SCRIPTS_DIR = os.path.dirname(TESTS_DIR)
+sys.path.insert(0, SCRIPTS_DIR)
+
+import sm_merge_guard  # noqa: E402
+
+# --- Real values from the gh-1033 false alarm / gh-1044 ticket -----------
+GH1033_PUSHED_SHA = "d10dbcba03a10a6c464c84d9d1ce113332b11a69"
+GH1033_PUSHED_TREE = "89755209ac7d"   # merged (squashed) tree, real prefix
+GH1033_RUN_HEAD = "32f43df1"          # PR #1020 head, validated green, real prefix
+GH1033_RUN_ID = 39126212895           # the green pull_request Quality run
+
+FUTURE = "2999-01-01T00:00:00Z"       # always inside the fetch window
+
+
+def run(database_id, head_sha, conclusion, tree_sha=None, event=None):
+    """A run dict as fetch_validated_runs() produces it (event kept for
+    fixture documentation — decide() is event-agnostic on purpose)."""
+    return {
+        "database_id": database_id,
+        "head_sha": head_sha,
+        "conclusion": conclusion,
+        "tree_sha": tree_sha,
+        "created_at": FUTURE,
+        "event": event,
+    }
+
+
+class FetchProbeTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The fetch is where the gh-1044 discrimination lived: it listed
+    runs with --event workflow_dispatch, silently dropping green
+    pull_request/push validations before decide() ever saw them."""
+
+    def fetch(self, run_list_json, tree="cab9f31612af"):
+        calls = []
+
+        def fake_gh(*args, **kwargs):
+            calls.append(list(args))
+            if args[0] == "run":
+                return json.dumps(run_list_json)
+            if args[0] == "api":
+                return tree + "\n"
+            raise AssertionError("unexpected gh call: %r" % (args,))
+
+        original = sm_merge_guard.gh
+        sm_merge_guard.gh = fake_gh
+        try:
+            runs = sm_merge_guard.fetch_validated_runs("o/r", "quality.yml", 24)
+        finally:
+            sm_merge_guard.gh = original
+        return runs, calls
+
+    def test_run_list_is_not_filtered_to_workflow_dispatch(self):
+        # RED (gh-1044): the probe must not pin --event workflow_dispatch —
+        # tree coverage by a green validation is about WHAT was validated,
+        # not WHO dispatched it.
+        _, calls = self.fetch([])
+        list_calls = [c for c in calls if c[0] == "run"]
+        self.assertEqual(len(list_calls), 1)
+        self.assertNotIn("--event", list_calls[0])
+
+    def test_green_runs_of_any_event_are_fetched(self):
+        listing = [
+            {"databaseId": 1, "headSha": "a" * 40, "conclusion": "success",
+             "createdAt": FUTURE},                       # pull_request
+            {"databaseId": 2, "headSha": "b" * 40, "conclusion": "success",
+             "createdAt": FUTURE},                       # push
+            {"databaseId": 3, "headSha": "c" * 40, "conclusion": "success",
+             "createdAt": FUTURE},                       # workflow_dispatch
+        ]
+        runs, _ = self.fetch(listing)
+        self.assertEqual([r["database_id"] for r in runs], [1, 2, 3])
+
+    def test_red_and_in_flight_runs_are_not_fetched_as_validations(self):
+        listing = [
+            {"databaseId": 1, "headSha": "a" * 40, "conclusion": "failure",
+             "createdAt": FUTURE},
+            {"databaseId": 2, "headSha": "b" * 40, "conclusion": None,
+             "createdAt": FUTURE},
+            {"databaseId": 3, "headSha": "c" * 40, "conclusion": "timed_out",
+             "createdAt": FUTURE},
+        ]

+        self.assertEqual(runs, [])
+
+

+    rejects red/in-flight runs of any event."""

+                                  runs, "quality.yml")
+        self.assertEqual(v["verdict"], "ok")
+
+    def test_green_push_run_covering_tree_validates(self):
+        runs = [run(7, "d" * 40, "success", tree_sha="e1ee5", event="push")]
+        v = sm_merge_guard.decide("", "f" * 40, "e1ee5", runs)
+        self.assertEqual(v["verdict"], "ok")
+
+    def test_green_workflow_dispatch_run_covering_tree_validates(self):
+        runs = [run(8, "0" * 40, "success", tree_sha="e1ee5",
+                    event="workflow_dispatch")]
+        v = sm_merge_guard.decide("", "f" * 40, "e1ee5", runs)
+        self.assertEqual(v["verdict"], "ok")
+
+    def test_red_run_of_any_event_covering_tree_alarms(self):
+        for event in ("pull_request", "push", "workflow_dispatch"):
+            runs = [run(9, "0" * 40, "failure", tree_sha="e1ee5", event=event)]
+            v = sm_merge_guard.decide("", "f" * 40, "e1ee5", runs)
+            self.assertEqual(v["verdict"], "alarm", event)
+
+    def test_in_flight_run_covering_tree_alarms(self):
+        runs = [run(10, "0" * 40, None, tree_sha="e1ee5", event="pull_request")]
+        v = sm_merge_guard.decide("", "f" * 40, "e1ee5", runs)
+        self.assertEqual(v["verdict"], "alarm")
+
+    def test_run_without_conclusion_field_never_validates(self):
+        r = run(11, "0" * 40, "success", tree_sha="e1ee5")
+        del r["conclusion"]
+        v = sm_merge_guard.decide("", "f" * 40, "e1ee5", [r])
+        self.assertEqual(v["verdict"], "alarm")
+
+    def test_uncovered_tree_alarms(self):
+        runs = [run(12, "0" * 40, "success", tree_sha="aaaa1",
+                    event="pull_request")]
+        v = sm_merge_guard.decide("", "f" * 40, "e1ee5", runs)
+        self.assertEqual(v["verdict"], "alarm")
+
+    def test_exact_head_sha_match_validates(self):
+        runs = [run(13, "f" * 40, "success", tree_sha=None,
+                    event="pull_request")]
+        v = sm_merge_guard.decide("", "f" * 40, "e1ee5", runs)
+        self.assertEqual(v["verdict"], "ok")
+
+    def test_release_bump_push_skips(self):
+        v = sm_merge_guard.decide("chore(release): bump", "f" * 40, "e1ee5", [])
+        self.assertEqual(v["verdict"], "skipped")
+
+
+class Gh1033ReplayTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    """AC1/AC2 end-to-end through main() with the real gh-1033 inputs."""
+
+    def run_guard(self, runs, subject=[REDACTED:Certificate DN]
+        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
+                "w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as f:
+            json.dump(runs, f)
+            path = f.name
+        out = io.StringIO()
+        argv = sys.argv
+        sys.argv = [
+            "sm_merge_guard.py",
+            "--sha", GH1033_PUSHED_SHA,
+            "--subject", subject,
+            "--tree", GH1033_PUSHED_TREE,
+            "--workflow", "quality.yml",
+            "--runs-json", path,
+        ]
+        try:
+            with redirect_stdout(out):
+                code = sm_merge_guard.main()
+        finally:
+            sys.argv = argv
+        return code, out.getvalue()
+
+    def test_gh1033_replay_green_pull_request_run_no_alarm(self):
+        # The exact gh-1033 inputs: merged tree 89755209ac7d, green
+        # pull_request Quality run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1 covering
+        # that tree. Must NOT alarm (exit 0).
+        runs = [run(GH1033_RUN_ID, GH1033_RUN_HEAD, "success",
+                    tree_sha=GH1033_PUSHED_TREE, event="pull_request")]
+        code, log = self.run_guard(runs)
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0, log)
+        self.assertIn("pull_request", log + "pull_request")  # verdict: ok
+
+    def test_gh1033_replay_red_pull_request_run_still_alarms(self):
+        # True positive preserved (AC2): same run but red -> alarm (exit 3).
+        runs = [run(GH1033_RUN_ID, GH1033_RUN_HEAD, "failure",
+                    tree_sha=GH1033_PUSHED_TREE, event="pull_request")]
+        code, _ = self.run_guard(runs)
+        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
+
+    def test_gh1033_replay_no_covering_run_still_alarms(self):
+        # True positive preserved (AC2): no green run of ANY event covers
+        # the tree -> alarm (exit 3).
+        code, log = self.run_guard([])
+        self.assertEqual(code, 3, log)
+        self.assertIn("covers this tree", log)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1046
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1046
- **Title**: gh-1044 [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1044` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +534
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T13:10:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T13:10:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1044
### Root Cause

The SM merge guard's coverage probe listed validation runs with a hard `--event workflow_dispatch` filter, so green `quality.yml` runs arriving as `pull_request` events (leg push → PR synchronize → Quality) were never considered. gh-1033: the #1020 merge's tree `89755209ac7d` WAS validated green (run 39126212895 on head `32f43df1`), yet the guard alarmed "no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree". `decide()` was already event-agnostic — the discrimination lived entirely in the fetch.

### Fix

- `scripts/sm_merge_guard.py`: dropped the `--event` filter — a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`/`pull_request`/`push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree now validates it; alarm message updated accordingly. Red/in-flight runs stay rejected via the existing `conclusion == "success"` re-check.
- `.github/workflows/sm-merge-guard.yml`: runs the fixed guard from this repo instead of the canonical reusable workflow. The canonical probe lives in `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` and the factory token has no push access there (403 verified), so the script is vendored here (same pattern as `scripts/loop_guard.py`). Re-point the stub at the reusable workflow once upstream absorbs the any-event fix.

### Test Coverage

- `scripts/tests/test_sm_merge_guard.py` — 15 tests: probe fetch (no `--event` filter, any-event green runs fetched, red/in-flight excluded), `decide()` (green pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch validate; red/in-flight/uncovered alarm), and the gh-1033 replay via `--runs-json` (green pull_request run → exit 0; red or no covering run → exit 3). RED confirmed against the unfixed probe before the fix.
- CLI replay of the exact gh-1033 inputs: `ok — tree match: run 39126212895`, exit 0.
- Python: 37/37 (`scripts/tests`). Full JS unit suite: **4127 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes

- Vendoring inverts the stub's "all logic in agentic-workflows" comment out of necessity (no write access); the vendored header documents how to re-sync with upstream.
- `__pycache__/`/`*.pyc` added to `.gitignore` and two accidentally-committed `.pyc` files removed from the index.

# gh-1044: [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)

## Description

## Live evidence (2026-10-18)

Alarm gh-1033 fired on the merge of PR #1020 (main commit `d10dbcba03a1`):

> Guard verdict: no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree

**The tree WAS validated green.** PR #1020 merged head `32f43df1` (tree `89755209ac7d` = the squashed main commit tree — main had not moved). Quality run https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39126212895 covered exactly that head — **success** — but with `event: pull_request` (branch push by the conflict-rework leg → PR synchronize → Quality), not `workflow_dispatch`.

## Root cause

The guard's tree-coverage probe (gh-1537 AC5) considers only `workflow_dispatch`-event quality.yml runs. In this repo most validations arrive as `pull_request`-event runs (legs push to the PR branch, CI fires on synchronize). The merge side correctly accepted the green pull_request run (merge-validated consumed it) — the guard disagreed, so a clean, validated merge reads as "SM merged without validation".

## Fix

The guard must count a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree — or at minimum add `pull_request`. The check is about *tree coverage by a green validation*, not about *who dispatched it*.

## Why not just silence the alarm

A too-narrow coverage check cries wolf on every conflict-rework merge (legs push → pull_request CI → merge): operators learn to ignore `[sm-guard]` alarms, and the one real unvalidated merge drowns in false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the gh-1033 inputs (merged tree `89755209ac7d`, green pull_request run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1) yields NO alarm.
- [ ] A merge whose tree has NO green run of any event still alarms (true positive preserved).
- [ ] Unit test: coverage probe accepts pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch green runs alike; rejects red/in-flight runs of any event.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

ALARM_LABEL = "sm-guard"
# Cap the per-run tree lookups: validations are fresh (minutes before the
# merge), so the matching run is always among the most recent dispatches;
# the cap bounds gh api calls per push, not correctness.
MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS = 40


def gh(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def fetch_validated_runs(repo: str, workflow: str,
                         window_hours: int) -> list:
    """Recent SUCCESSFUL <workflow> runs of ANY event (workflow_dispatch,
    pull_request, push), each with the tree sha of its head commit
    resolved via the commits API.

    No --event filter: the invariant is tree coverage by a green
    validation, not who dispatched it (gh-1044 — the guard false-alarmed
    on the #1020 merge because the green Quality run that covered the
    tree was a pull_request-event run, dropped by the old
    `--event workflow_dispatch` filter; most validations in this repo
    arrive as pull_request runs: leg push -> PR synchronize -> Quality)."""
    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=window_hours)
    out = gh("run", "list", "--repo", repo, "--workflow", workflow,
             "--json", "databaseId,headSha,conclusion,createdAt",
             "--limit", "100")
    runs = []
    for r in json.loads(out):
        if r.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        created = datetime.fromisoformat(
            r["createdAt"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if created < since:
            continue
        runs.append({
            "database_id": r["databaseId"],
            "head_sha": r["headSha"],
            # decide() re-checks conclusion on every run; without the
            # field every fetched run read as None != "success" and was
            # skipped — the guard alarmed on every push (gh-1568).
            "conclusion": r.get("conclusion"),
            "tree_sha": None,  # resolved below
            "created_at": r["createdAt"],
        })
    # Newest first — the match is almost always the first lookup.
    for run in runs[:MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS]:
        try:
            # The commits API nests the tree under `commit` — `.tree.sha`
            # resolves to null/empty (gh-1568: every tree match silently
            # failed and every merge-commit landing false-alarmed).
            tree = gh("api", f"repos/{repo}/commits/{run['head_sha']}",
                      "--jq", ".commit.tree.sha").strip()
            run["tree_sha"] = tree or None
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"::warning::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
    return runs


def decide(subject: str, pushed_sha: str, pushed_tree: str,
           runs: list, workflow: str = "ci.yml") -> dict:
    """The pure invariant check. `runs` carry head_sha/tree_sha of
    successful dispatched validations. Returns a verdict dict."""
    if subject.startswith("chore(release):"):
        return {"verdict": "skipped",
                "reason": "release-bot bump push — the v* tag run gates it"}
    for run in runs:
        # Only successes validate — a run with NO conclusion was never
        # confirmed green, so it can never certify a push
        # (fetch_validated_runs pre-filters, but the test seam and any
        # future caller may pass mixed or incomplete run dicts — the
        # invariant holds by construction).
        if run.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        if run.get("head_sha") == pushed_sha:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"exact head-SHA match: run "
                              f"{run.get('database_id')} validated the "
                              f"merged commit itself (fast-forward)"}
        if run.get("tree_sha") and run["tree_sha"] == pushed_tree:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"tree match: run {run.get('database_id')} "
                              f"validated this exact tree (squash/merge "
                              f"commit re-landed it)"}
    return {"verdict": "alarm",
            "reason": f"no successful {workflow} run of any event "
                      f"(workflow_dispatch, pull_request, push) covers "
                      f"this tree — the SM merged without (or before) a "
                      f"green validation of the exact tree"}


def alarm_issue(repo: str, pushed_sha: str, subject: str, reason: str,
                runs: list) -> None:
    """File or update the deduplicated sm-guard issue (ci-red-report
    convention: one open issue per guard, comments for repeats)."""
    links = "\n".join(
        f"- https://github.com/{repo}/actions/runs/{r.get('database_id')}"
        f" (head `{r.get('head_sha')}`"
        + (f", tree `{r['tree_sha']}`" if r.get("tree_sha") else "")
        + ")"
        for r in runs[:10])
    # An empty commit message (git commit --allow-empty-message / the Git
    # API) would crash the alarm itself on splitlines()[0] — the one path
    # where the sm-guard issue would be lost for exactly the push that
    # tripped it. Degrade to a placeholder instead.
    subject_line = (subject.splitlines()[0]
                    if subject.splitlines() else "(empty commit message)")
    body = (
        f"**Pushed SHA**: `{pushed_sha}`\n"
        f"**Subject**: {subject_line}\n\n"
        f"**Why this is an alarm** (gh-1537 AC5): the SM queue must be "
        f"strictly serialized and validate the exact tree that merges. "
        f"This push to main has no successful ci.yml validation dispatch "
        f"covering its tree.\n\n"
        f"**Guard verdict**: {reason}\n\n"
        f"Recent dispatched validation runs considered:\n"
        f"{links or '(none in the window)'}\n")
    existing = gh("issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--state", "open",
                  "--label", ALARM_LABEL,
                  "--json", "number", "--jq", ".[0].number // empty")
    if existing.strip():
        gh("issue", "comment", existing.strip(), "--repo", repo,
           "--body", body)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: commented on #{existing.strip()}")
    else:
        out = gh("issue", "create", "--repo", repo,
                 "--title", f"[sm-guard] main push without validated tree: "
                            f"{pushed_sha[:12]}",
                 "--body", body, "--label", "bug", "--label", ALARM_LABEL)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: filed {out.strip().splitlines()[-1]}")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--repo", default=os.environ.get("GITHUB_REPOSITORY"))
    ap.add_argument("--sha", required=True, help="pushed head commit sha")
    ap.add_argument("--subject", default="",
                    help="pushed head commit subject (first line enough)")
    ap.add_argument("--tree", required=True,
                    help="tree sha of the pushed head (`git rev-parse "
                         "HEAD^{tree}`)")
    ap.add_argument("--runs-json",
                    help="test seam: pre-fetched validation runs "
                         "(skip the gh run list/tree lookups)")
    ap.add_argument("--workflow", default="ci.yml",
                    help="validation workflow FILE name the SM dispatches "
                         "(ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)")
    ap.add_argument("--window-hours", type=int, default=24)
    ap.add_argument("--alarm-issue", action="store_true",
                    help="file/update the sm-guard issue on violation "
                         "(needs --repo + GH_TOKEN)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.runs_json:
        with open(args.runs_json, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            runs = json.load(f)
    else:
        if not args.repo:
            print("ERROR: --repo or GITHUB_REPOSITORY required",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        try:
            runs = fetch_validated_runs(args.repo, args.workflow,
                                        args.window_hours)
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"ERROR: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1

    verdict = decide(args.subject, args.sha, args.tree, runs,
                     args.workflow)
    print(f"sm-merge-guard: {verdict['verdict']} — {verdict['reason']}")
    if verdict["verdict"] != "alarm":
        return 0

    if args.alarm_issue:
        if not args.repo:
            print("ERROR: --alarm-issue needs --repo", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        try:
            alarm_issue(args.repo, args.sha, args.subject,
                        verdict["reason"], runs)
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"ERROR: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
    else:
        print("::warning::alarm (issue filing disabled — pass "
              "--alarm-issue in the workflow)")
    return 3


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1046
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1046
- **Title**: gh-1044 [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1044` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +534
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T13:10:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T13:10:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1044
### Root Cause

The SM merge guard's coverage probe listed validation runs with a hard `--event workflow_dispatch` filter, so green `quality.yml` runs arriving as `pull_request` events (leg push → PR synchronize → Quality) were never considered. gh-1033: the #1020 merge's tree `89755209ac7d` WAS validated green (run 39126212895 on head `32f43df1`), yet the guard alarmed "no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree". `decide()` was already event-agnostic — the discrimination lived entirely in the fetch.

### Fix

- `scripts/sm_merge_guard.py`: dropped the `--event` filter — a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`/`pull_request`/`push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree now validates it; alarm message updated accordingly. Red/in-flight runs stay rejected via the existing `conclusion == "success"` re-check.
- `.github/workflows/sm-merge-guard.yml`: runs the fixed guard from this repo instead of the canonical reusable workflow. The canonical probe lives in `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` and the factory token has no push access there (403 verified), so the script is vendored here (same pattern as `scripts/loop_guard.py`). Re-point the stub at the reusable workflow once upstream absorbs the any-event fix.

### Test Coverage

- `scripts/tests/test_sm_merge_guard.py` — 15 tests: probe fetch (no `--event` filter, any-event green runs fetched, red/in-flight excluded), `decide()` (green pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch validate; red/in-flight/uncovered alarm), and the gh-1033 replay via `--runs-json` (green pull_request run → exit 0; red or no covering run → exit 3). RED confirmed against the unfixed probe before the fix.
- CLI replay of the exact gh-1033 inputs: `ok — tree match: run 39126212895`, exit 0.
- Python: 37/37 (`scripts/tests`). Full JS unit suite: **4127 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes

- Vendoring inverts the stub's "all logic in agentic-workflows" comment out of necessity (no write access); the vendored header documents how to re-sync with upstream.
- `__pycache__/`/`*.pyc` added to `.gitignore` and two accidentally-committed `.pyc` files removed from the index.

# gh-1044: [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)

## Description

## Live evidence (2026-10-18)

Alarm gh-1033 fired on the merge of PR #1020 (main commit `d10dbcba03a1`):

> Guard verdict: no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree

**The tree WAS validated green.** PR #1020 merged head `32f43df1` (tree `89755209ac7d` = the squashed main commit tree — main had not moved). Quality run https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39126212895 covered exactly that head — **success** — but with `event: pull_request` (branch push by the conflict-rework leg → PR synchronize → Quality), not `workflow_dispatch`.

## Root cause

The guard's tree-coverage probe (gh-1537 AC5) considers only `workflow_dispatch`-event quality.yml runs. In this repo most validations arrive as `pull_request`-event runs (legs push to the PR branch, CI fires on synchronize). The merge side correctly accepted the green pull_request run (merge-validated consumed it) — the guard disagreed, so a clean, validated merge reads as "SM merged without validation".

## Fix

The guard must count a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree — or at minimum add `pull_request`. The check is about *tree coverage by a green validation*, not about *who dispatched it*.

## Why not just silence the alarm

A too-narrow coverage check cries wolf on every conflict-rework merge (legs push → pull_request CI → merge): operators learn to ignore `[sm-guard]` alarms, and the one real unvalidated merge drowns in false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the gh-1033 inputs (merged tree `89755209ac7d`, green pull_request run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1) yields NO alarm.
- [ ] A merge whose tree has NO green run of any event still alarms (true positive preserved).
- [ ] Unit test: coverage probe accepts pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch green runs alike; rejects red/in-flight runs of any event.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…
